Subject: SOC 2 Type II + sample evidence request

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. As part of our vendor security review for the integration, our compliance team asked for your latest SOC 2 Type II report and a few targeted artifacts so our auditors can validate controls for authentication and access management. Specifically we need:

- SOC 2 Type II report (most recent) and any bridge letter if the report period doesn't cover calendar 2026.
- A 30-day slice of MFA/access logs that covers at least one month within your SOC 2 period (UTC timestamps are fine).
- Recent access review exports for privileged groups (CSV) and the documented procedure used to run them.
- Confirmation of whether usernames in logs are raw usernames or pseudonymized/hashed.

Can you confirm what you can provide and an estimated delivery date? We can accept redacted PII in the slices as long as there is a consistent identifier for mapping in our audit.

Appreciate it,
Liam
Security Operations
Hearthwell Health

--

Hi Liam,

Thanks — we can help. High level: we will share our most recent SOC 2 Type II report and provide a bridge letter if the report window doesn't overlap your audit period. We can also provide scoped artifacts for authentication controls (MFA) and access reviews with limited redaction.

One clarification before we prepare the extracts: what exact audit window do your auditors need the slice to cover? You mentioned "at least one month" — do you want a specific calendar month (e.g., Dec 2026) or a rolling 30-day window that intersects our SOC 2 period? Also: do you require raw usernames or are pseudonymized identifiers acceptable?

Tentative timeline: SOC 2 report + bridge letter (if needed) within 3 business days; scoped artifact extracts within 5 business days after we confirm the exact window and acceptable redaction rules. We will provide a downloadable Drive folder and share a HubSpot link for tracking.

I will loop in Marissa from compliance to handle the artifacts and Monica from CS for the delivery plan.

Best,

Hi Liam — Marissa on the compliance team here. Quick plan to get you everything your auditors asked for: 

1) SOC 2 material: attaching a one-page summary of our SOC 2 Type II (redwood_soc2_type2_summary_2024.pdf) for immediate review. We will provide the full report and a bridge letter (if necessary) via Drive by EOD Friday (15 Jan).

2) MFA/access logs: we can export a CSV slice for Dec 01 2026 — Jan 10 2027 (UTC) which overlaps our audit window. That file will include an event timestamp, event type (auth_attempt, mfa_challenge, mfa_success, mfa_failure), and an opaque subject_id (hashed) rather than raw username to protect PII. If your auditors require mapping, we can discuss a signed NDA and a secure process for mapping identifiers.

3) Access reviews: attaching a sample export of a privileged group review and our process doc excerpt. The export (access_review_sample_export_202612.xlsx) contains usernames replaced with the same opaque subject_id used in the log slice so auditors can cross-reference events.

4) Retention/controls confirmation: our log retention policy keeps auth logs for 24 months in compressed archival storage; live indexes hold 90 days. We will include a short statement in the bridge letter.

Timeline: SOC 2 report + bridge letter — by 2027-01-15. MFA log slice + access review export — by 2027-01-18. If you are comfortable with hashed identifiers we will proceed; if you need raw usernames we will need an executed NDA and procurement request for additional security review (adds 3–5 business days).

Attachments (for now): redwood_soc2_type2_summary_2024.pdf, access_review_sample_export_202612.xlsx

Let me know if the Dec01–Jan10 window works for your audit and whether the hashed-subject approach is acceptable.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Compliance
Redwood Inference
